findings.title: P1: doctor/CLI ignore compose.yml not owned by the target repo
findings.body: The `_owned_compose` helper correctly ensures that explicit `compose_path` resolves to a child of `repo_path`. Foreign `compose.yml` files are correctly ignored, preventing product-compose convention hazards.

findings.title: P2: mcp up returns without docker compose up if empty service list
findings.body: If `task-orchestrator` is removed due to a missing `DOPECON_BRIDGE_TOKEN` and the `svc_list` becomes empty, the CLI correctly returns early with a warning rather than running an empty `docker compose up`.

findings.title: P3: configured_ports None-narrowing
findings.body: Safe-guard logic added to check `configured_ports is not None` before querying it, preventing potential TypeErrors/KeyErrors during diagnostic generation.

findings.title: P4: test line wrap
findings.body: Test line wrap formatting fixes implemented, tests pass.

findings.title: Original Formula-Reserved WARN Behavior
findings.body: Formula collisions correctly downgrade from `FAIL` to `WARN` if `source_label == "formula"` and the user has safely overridden the collision with a non-reserved port via `.envrc`. Configured reserved collisions remain `FAIL`.

findings.title: Secrets handling
findings.body: No secrets are written to `.mcp.json` or `.env`. The fix for compose interpolation injects a dummy string `dopemux-compose-interpolation-only` which is safe.

findings.title: Scope constraint validation
findings.body: All changes were restricted to the allowlist provided in TP-DMX-MCP-DOCTOR-FORMULA-RESERVED-001.json.

fixes_applied: mcp up returns gracefully on empty service list
remaining_risks: If a user bypasses dopemux and directly invokes `docker compose up task-orchestrator` with the fake token `dopemux-compose-interpolation-only`, it could parse successfully but fail at runtime. This is an expected side effect of the fix.
The `_owned_compose` check relies on `repo_path` being accurate. Symlinked worktrees could potentially cause edge cases.
